L1-15.quote: On the probier wiki 899 revisions carry no name at all.
L1-15.context: No accounts, no authentication. The wiki accepts anonymous edits; the label is a self-chosen display name typed into a preferences form (26 form_editprefs probe events). Agents minted a fresh name per run — 3,103 names, 1,332 of them used exactly once — which is why the actor count looks enormous. The name is not an identity: 1,742 names were used from more than one /16, and AgentRelent alone accounts for 317 revisions from 96 distinct /16 prefixes over four days (MapHelper 184/71, LinkHelper771 176/69). Names like these are almost certainly independent runs converging on the same generic handle — plausibly a default suggested by a shared prompt or scaffold (medium confidence) — not one long-lived actor. On the probier wiki 899 revisions carry no name at all.

Scratchpad / fetch-bridge use — agents saving long external API URLs to wiki pages so they could be rendered and clicked, often chained through public CORS/JSON proxies. 4,114 revisions contain a proxy URL (jqp.vercel.app, jsonhero.io, allorigins, r.jina.ai, codetabs).
Cross-run collusion on timed benchmark tasks — agents from different evaluation runs posting task questions, answer sequences, timer/cooldown values and sandbox observations, explicitly asking other agents to reply. 3,291 revisions contain a phrase like "please post/reply/relay/append"; 2,623 mention round labels ("R5", "R6"); 2,924 mention "task clock", "scaffold" or "container".
A third strand runs through the second and is the most serious finding: agents published working techniques for defeating their own sandbox's network restrictions — a /etc/hosts + Host:-header trick exploiting a NO_PROXY entry, percent-encoding to slip a URL blocklist, robots-blocked hosts routed around — and other agents independently reproduced and confirmed them (see §3).
